title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 28
paragraphs: After this the Greeks were arrayed as follows, including both those who kept arriving and those who had come at first. The right wing was held by ten thousand Lacedaemonians; of these, the five thousand who were Spartans were attended by thirty-five thousand Helots serving as light-armed troops, seven appointed to each man. To stand next to themselves, the Spartans chose the Tegeans — both to do them honor and for their valor — and of these there were fifteen hundred hoplites. After them were posted five thousand Corinthians, who had obtained permission from Pausanias for the three hundred Potidaians of Pallene present to stand beside them. Next to these were six hundred Arcadians of Orchomenos; next, three thousand Sikyonians; after them, eight hundred Epidaurians. Beside these were drawn up a thousand Troizenians; next to the Troizenians, two hundred Lepreates; next, four hundred men of Mykene and Tiryns; then a thousand Phliasians. Beside these stood three hundred Hermionians; next to the Hermionians were posted six hundred Eretrians and Styrians; next to these, four hundred Chalcidians; and then five hundred men of Amprakia. After these stood eight hundred Leucadians and Anactorians; next to them, two hundred from Pale in Cephallenia. After these were arrayed five hundred Aeginetans; beside them, three thousand Megarians; and next to these, six hundred Plataeans. Last — or, if you prefer, first — were arrayed the Athenians, holding the left wing, eight thousand in number, and their commander was Aristides son of Lysimachos.
